units.text: INT. RIDESHARE CAR - MOVING - NIGHT
2:07 AM on the dashboard clock.

DEV PATEL, 30s, a driver with four stars and a lanyard from his real job still around his neck, steers through empty wet streets while a HOODIE GUY in the back seat hugs a gym bag, and a woman in the passenger seat, NADIA, 20s, who ordered the ride and keeps checking her phone, says nothing, and the app chirps, and Dev smiles at the mirror like a man who has read a lot of tips about conversation.
Big night? Or, early morning, I guess.
units.name: DEV

units.text: Just drive.
units.name: HOODIE GUY

units.text: Dev's phone, mounted on the dash, lights up with a Slack message ON SCREEN: "#ops-standup - Brenda: reminder, Q3 retro at 9.
Cameras ON please."
Cameras on. At nine. Sure.
units.name: DEV

units.text: Nadia's phone rings.
She answers on speaker, and a man's voice comes through, thin and furious.
Where are you? You said you'd have it by two.
units.name: LUKE

units.text: We're coming. Stop calling.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Is that him in the car? Is that the guy?
units.name: LUKE

units.text: The Hoodie Guy lowers his hood.

He is maybe nineteen, scared, and holding the bag as though it might go off, and the streetlights flick over all three of them in turn, orange and then dark, until Dev finally understands that this is not a ride.
Show him it, Marcus.
units.name: NADIA

units.text: Marcus unzips the bag.
Stacks of cash, banded.
Dev brakes hard, the car SLIDES, the phone clatters from its mount.
This is the last time any of them will be strangers.
I have a daughter. I have a performance review.
units.name: DEV

units.text: Somebody say something!
units.name: LUKE
